    <item>
      <title>Utbrudd av influensa: – Ta vaksinen nå</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/utbrudd-av-influensa_-_-ta-vaksinen-na-1.18089136</link>
      <description>Vinterens influensautbrudd er i gang. Samtidig øker koronasmitten.
Det opplyser Folkehelseinstituttet torsdag.
– Beskyttelse mot influensa og covid-19 oppnås én til to uker etter at du har tatt vaksine. Det er derfor viktig at de som er anbefalt vaksine tar den nå, før smitten øker ytterligere, sier overlege Ingvild Fjeldheim ved FHI.
Vaksine er det viktigste tiltaket for å beskytte risikogrupper og eldre mot alvorlig influensa- og koronasykdom, heter det.
Men forsinkelser i leveransene har ført til at enkelte kommuner har måttet vente med vaksineringen. Dette problemet skal imidlertid være løst nå.
– Har du måtte utsette vaksineringen fordi vaksinen ikke var tilgjengelig, oppfordrer vi deg til å ta vaksine nå, sier Fjeldheim.
Disse anbefales å ta influensavaksinen:
• Alle fra fylte 65 år.
• Barn og voksne i definerte risikogrupper.
• Gravide etter 12. svangerskapsuke, og tidligere i svangerskapet ved tilleggsrisiko.
• Helsepersonell med nær pasientkontakt.</description>

      <pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 12:14:16 GMT</pubDate>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nusa-dobbel-for-leipzig-i-meisterligaen-1.18088054</link>
      <description>Antonio Nusa briljerte med heile to scoringar for RB Leipzig i kampen mot franske Lens.
Nusa markerte seg allereie frå start og sørga for det andre av to mål for Leipzig i første omgang før det var gått ti minutt.
Etter pausen var franskmennene litt meir på ballen og fekk utteljing då Matthieu Udol plukka opp ein retur etter eit blokkert skot og sette ballen i mål.
Mot slutten sette Leipzig alle mann i angrep og Nusa fekk ein enkel jobb med å setta si andre scoring, få sekund før dommaren blåste av kampen.
Stillinga blei til slutt 3–1 til tyskarane, medan Lens held fram med skuffande resultat.
Den franske klubben vann den første kampen i Meisterligaen i haust, men har sidan gått på fire strake tap.
9. desember møter dei Bodø/Glimt på heimebane.
Martin Ødegaard og Arsenal spelte uavgjort mot Borussia Dortmund og Julian Ryerson.
Det same gjorde Manchester City som klarte å utlikna til 2–2 mot Napoli i det 86. speleminuttet, sjølv om Erling Braut Haaland var mållaus gjennom heile kampen.</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/skandalen-i-afrikamesterskapet_-senegal-far-tilbake-tittelen-1.18087604</link>
      <description>Idrettens voldgiftsrett (CAS) har konkludert med at Senegal gjeninnsettes som vinnere av Afrikamesterskapet i fotball i 2025.
Det har Idrettens voldgiftsrett besluttet, ifølge nyhetskanalen Reuters.
Det er nesten ti måneder siden Senegal forlot banen i protest da vertsnasjon Marokko fikk straffespark på overtid i finalen. Kampen ble stoppet i nærmere et kvarter.
Marokkos Brahim Díaz bommet, og Senegal vant kampen 1-0 etter ekstraomganger.
Det afrikanske fotballforbundet (CAF) ga først ut bøter og utestengelser til Senegal.
I mars ble Senegal fratatt tittelen og Marokko tilkjent 3-0 og seier. Senegals fotballforbund anket saken til CAS.
I oktober ble det gjennomført en høring bak lukkede dører.
Tirsdag kom den endelige kjennelsen i tvisten.
Senegal møtte Norge i gruppespillet i VM i USA i sommer. Der vant Norge 3-2 etter en dramatisk avslutning.
(NTB)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Ingen utsatt frist for de rødgrønne: Må avklare innen onsdag</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/ingen-utsatt-frist-for-de-rodgronne_-ma-avklare-innen-onsdag-1.18087741</link>
      <description>Finanskomiteen på Stortinget fastholder at fristen for å melde inn politiske forslag og omprioriteringer til statsbudsjettet utløper klokken 10 i morgen, onsdag.
Komiteen hadde et kort møte i dag klokken 13, der det ikke ble gjort endringer i fremdriftsplanen som gjelder for behandlingen av budsjettet på Stortinget.
I praksis betyr dette at budsjettforhandlingene på rødgrønn side må få en avklaring i løpet av dagen, kvelden eller natta. Dermed øker presset på de fem partiene som har forhandlet om statsbudsjettet siden 6. november.
En avklaring må ikke nødvendigvis innebære en budsjettavtale med et avklart flertall bak seg. I fjor la Ap, Rødt og Senterpartiet fram en avtale, som ikke hadde flertall. SV og MDG kom først om bord noen dager senere.</description>
      <category domain="emphasis">high</category>
      <pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 12:19:39 GMT</pubDate>

      <description>To personer ble natt til mandag pågrepet av svensk politi i forbindelse med voldshendelsen i Alta søndag morgen, skriver politiet i loggen.
De to personene er bosatt et annet sted i Norge, siktet for drapsforsøk mot en mann bosatt i Alta.
Politiet etterforsker nå bakgrunnen for at de to dro til Alta og oppsøkte den fornærmede.
Etterforskningen så langt har avdekket at det har vært en relasjon mellom partene fra tidligere av.

Avgjørelsen kommer etter samtaler og møter med Huang, opplyser selskapet i en pressemelding.

      <description>120 avviste asylsøkere i Danmark oppfyller kriteriene for å bli sendt til et retursenter i Rwanda neste år.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/karoline-grotting-best-av-alle-pa-sesongapningens-siste-dag-_-skiskytter-imponerte-1.18086614</link>
      <description>Karoline Grøtting var best av samtlige kvinner under dagens 15 kilometer fristil på Beitostølen.
5 kilometer før mål sto kampen om seieren mellom Grøtting og Kristin Austgulen Fosnæs. Der var det altså Grøtting som til slutt trakk det lengste strået.
Grøtting stod over fredagens 10 kilometer på grunn av magesmerter i et forsøk på å spare seg til dagens distanse.
– Jeg er veldig glad for det nå, sier Grøtting til NRK etter målgang.
Skiskytter Ida Lien var dagens andre startende og gikk i mål til ledelse. Der ble hun værende til Grøtting overtok lederstolen.
Likevel holdt det til 3. plass for skiskytteren.
Heidi Weng vant fredagens 10 kilometer klassisk, men klarte ikke å gjenskape prestasjonen i dag. Allerede ved 6,2 kilometer hadde Weng 17 sekunder opp til teten.
Weng endte på 5. plass, 36 sekunder bak vinner.
Herrene skal ut på sin 15 kilometer klokken 13:00. Den kan du følge på NRK TV.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Selvik reddet straffe på overtid da Brest vant igjen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/selvik-reddet-straffe-pa-overtid-da-brest-vant-igjen-1.18086449</link>
      <description>Egil Selvik fortsetter å storspille i Brest-målet. Lørdag sikret han 1-0-seier borte mot Strasbourg ved å redde straffespark fem minutter på overtid.
Sraffen ble dømt etter en VAR-gjennomgang av en situasjon der ballen traff armen til Brest-spiller Mama Baldé, men det berget ikke hjemmelaget.
Brest tok ledelsen ved Noah Edjouma i det 22. minutt, etter en svak klarering av keeper Filip Jørgensen. Selvik forsvarte ledelsen med en rekke gode redninger og hjalp laget sitt til den tredje strake seieren i Ligue 1.
Selvik voktet Norges mål i nasjonsligaseieren over Wales for en uke siden, men han måtte overraskende sette seg på benken igjen da Norge knep gruppeseieren med 3-2-seier over Danmark i Parken tirsdag. Da var Ørjan Nyland tilbake i målet. Lørdag satt Nyland på benken for RB Leipzig.
Brest-seieren løftet laget til 6.-plass på tabellen. Strasbourg har bare tre lag bak seg på tabellen.
(©NTB)</description>

An Ontario man has been sentenced to more than four years in prison after getting caught at Vancouver International Airport with a “significant amount” of methamphetamine in his luggage.

Mounties say in a release that the investigation began on Aug. 29, 2024, when officials from the Canada Border Services Agency stopped the man before he was to board a flight to New Zealand. 

Police say a search of his checked luggage uncovered 15 kilograms of methamphetamine, and the man was arrested then released pending further investigation.

RCMP say 29-year-old Joshua Bryant has since pleaded guilty in provincial court in Richmond, B.C., to importing and exporting controlled substances and possessing a controlled drug for the purpose of trafficking. 

Bryant was sentenced to four-and-a-half years in custody last Friday, and the court has also imposed a 10-year firearms prohibition. 

Ana Maria Coutu, director of CBSA’s Vancouver International Airport District, says in a statement that the seizure stopped a “significant amount of methamphetamine from endangering communities in New Zealand” in the authorities’ efforts to disrupt cross-border drug trafficking.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 26, 2026.

Disposal fees at the Hartland Landfill are about to increase for certain materials, effective Jan. 1, 2027, as part of the Capital Regional District’s larger plan to minimize and divert waste from the region’s only solid waste landfill.

The increase applies to general garbage, clean wood, treated wood, asphalt singles and yard and garden waste.

The fee increases are listed below:

  • General refuse: from $160/tonne to $165/tonne
  • Clean wood: from $80/tonne to $95/tonne
  • Treated wood: from $110/tonne to $150/tonne
  • Asphalt shingles: from $110/tonne to $160/tonne
  • Yard and garden waste: from $59/tonne to $65/tonne

Hartland Landfill implements material bans in 2024

Hartland changed its policy in 2024, banning several construction materials from regular garbage disposal and implementing a tipping fee to take them offsite for recycling.

The materials included asphalt shingles, treated wood, salvageable wood and carpet and underlay.

“The changes aim to help divert 40,500 tonnes of material annually, contributing to a reduction of over one-third of the region’s waste,” stated the district in 2024.

READ RELATED: Trash to treasure: New program aims to reuse construction waste on Vancouver Island

In the summer of 2025, the CRD alerted the public to planned yearly hikes in tipping fees for general garbage disposal.

Between 2026 and 2028, yearly general waste fees are set to increase by $15.

The district says annual increases will bring in an estimated $3.85 million in revenue and will be put towards continued waste reduction initiatives.

Waste reduction initiatives across the Island, province

The material bans are part of a larger CRD plan to minimize waste disposal at Hartland and increase the number of materials diverted to recycling sites.

By 2050, the CRD estimates the Hartland Landfill will have reached capacity.

Across the province, 226 landfills are managed by 27 regional districts and 161 municipalities, each faced with the task of diverting waste from the aging landfills.

B.C.’s zero waste and circular economy plan includes a province-wide disposal target of 350 kilograms of municipal solid waste per person annually.

The CRD has a plan to surpass the provincial target; 250 kg per person per year by 2031. It’s part of the CRD’s Solid Waste Management Plan (SWMP).

Capital residents are already chipping away at this target. CRD residents disposed of 330 kg per person in 2025, showing a decrease of 8 kg per capita from 2024, according to the latest SWMP progress report.  The average waste total per person combined amounts to a total of 150,441 tonnes of waste received and disposed of by the Hartland Landfill in 2025.

In 2024, residents in the Capital Regional District had the lowest per-person annual waste disposal (341 kg/person) across B.C., according to Environmental Reporting B.C.

Published in July 2026, the province-wide indicator shows how waste was disposed of across B.C. between 1990 to 2024.

The Peace River Regional District, a bustling region for industry in Northern B.C., reported the highest per person annual waste disposal (763 kg/person).

Communities across the Island are doubling down on waste-reducing initiatives, including a plan to reduce single-use waste in the Regional District of Nanaimo, a curbside program in the Cowichan Valley, and cost-cutting waste collection initiatives in Langford.

READ RELATED:

  • RDN launches Sip Smart Challenge to reduce single-use waste
  • Cowichan Valley curbside program cuts landfill waste by nearly 27%
  • Langford considers municipal garbage collection to cut costs for residents

Alongside B.C.’s districts and municipalities searching for long-term solutions, the CRD has several initiatives underway, including the launch of Hartland 2050+, which examines exploring a range of waste disposal options, including landfill alternatives, for the future.

Beyond the Curb recycling drop-offs also launched this year, completing 250 days of curbside service for recyclable materials collected from single-family homes.

More progress updates are provided in the district’s Solid Waste Recycling Community Need Summary 2027.

Situated about 14 kilometres northwest of Victoria, the Hartland Landfill serves an estimated 440,000 people and is the only solid waste disposal facility in the Capital Region.

The Peninsula Community Pickleball Club has eyes on Victoria Airport Authority lands to build an indoor facility.

“We are a local group of pickleball players who recognise a desperate need for a community asset out here on the Peninsula for a place to play that’s sheltered for the eight months of the year that we can’t play on outdoor courts, which we are also short of, by the way,” Cindy Barton, president of the pickleball club, said in a Zoom interview.

“But money doesn’t go as far as it used to, so we figured we’d get our biggest bang for our buck and cover eight courts with a steel truss and tension fabric coated structure to make an indoor pickleball facility.”

The facility is being planned for the Victoria Airport Authority lands near Rotary Park, which Barton says will help address some of the noise concerns people have with the sport.

“We’re looking to build on Victoria Airport land, right at the end of a runway, where there’s more commercial noise there than pickleball noise, and then we are looking at even lining that building. A 2025 survey by Pickleball Canada showed the sport continues to attract new players, with an estimated 1.54 million Canadians playing the sport, up 57 per cent from 2022.

That popularity can make it hard to find court space.

Barton says indoor courts are sparse, with players using a number of spaces that are built for a variety of sports, meaning they may not have the right spacing or other considerations for pickleball.

Victoria council has unanimously passed two advocacy motions, asking for stiffer penalties for dangerous drivers, and for the B.C. government to reconsider relocating its offices.

The motion for increased accountability for dangerous drivers was passed on the consent agenda, and the government offices motion was pulled from the consent for Coun. Matt Dell to recuse himself.

Dangerous driving penalties and enforcement

Council unanimously approved a motion in committee of the whole calling to advocate to the federal and provincial governments for:

  • Stricter penalties for driving without due care and attention.
  • Increasing the number of red-light and speed cameras.
  • Create a new category of offence that better addresses careless, reckless or negligent driving resulting in bodily harm.
  • Direct Crown counsel to more frequently propose the dangerous driving causing death charge.

This push is coming after a cyclist, Sylvie Argouarch, was killed on Quadra Street by a driver who ran a red light. The driver, Dugan Ian Ingram, was given the maximum sentence for driving without due care and attention: a $2,000 fine and two-year driving ban.

“At its heart, it’s a motion to try to improve the safety for Victoria residents. We’ve seen some really tragic incidents recently. And safety is required from all three levels of government: municipal, provincial and federal,” Thompson said on Nov. 24.

Coun. Jack Sandor said the goal is to penalize drivers with repeated infractions.

“The fact is, not to punish people with a good history of driving for one simple, small mistake. The point is to identify people who have clearly shown a pattern of being repeat offenders, of being dangerous drivers,” Sandor said on Nov. 24.

Call on B.C. government to keep its offices downtown Victoria

As the B.C. government begins to implement its return-to-office mandate, questions are arising about where the employees will work.

A motion by Couns. Stephen Hammond and Melissa Cseszko note that a message to then-Ministry of Transportation and Transit staff indicated that they will be moved from a downtown Victoria office building to a Saanich building.

Planned equipment upgrades at the Victoria Curling Club have come up short of the hog line this season, as waiting on delayed equipment to arrive threatened to wipe out the club’s annual operating budget.  

James Keough, the club’s general manager, says the club has been in need of major upgrades for several years.

After consulting, the club came up with a plan to install a new refrigeration system with an estimated cost of $850,000.

“We knew what we needed to do and had most of the system designed, and we needed to raise the funds,” said Keough.

The club raised $500,000 through its members, and the remaining amount came through other fundraising initiatives, including a city grant.

By late April 2026, major equipment had been ordered was expected to arrive in August 2026. The curling season starts in September.

“We were informed midway through the summer that a couple of the pieces of equipment were delayed,” said Keough.

The delays were for a new chiller, which is the refrigeration piece, and a fluid cooler.

“We knew that they would take the longest to arrive to be built and delivered,” said Keough.

“So we had to make a decision as to whether we were going to use an old plant or delay our season and wait for the new ones to arrive,” says Keough.

In curling terms, the club had to pick a line, and decided to save the upcoming season and take a chance on the existing plant, and make repairs as needed.

Keough says the new equipment was expected to arrive between late December to February 2027.

“We would have lost our entire curling season,” he says. “We curl from September through April, and during the curling season, we run 20 leagues, as well as youth programs, Special Olympics, school visits, learn to curl programs, as well as special events like bonspiels.”

Waiting for the equipment would have a significant financial impact on the club he says.

READ RELATED: Victoria Curling Club racing to replace aging ice-making plant before next season

“Our entire budget is $500,000, so basically all of our annual operating expenses. It would have been a very significant blow to the existence of the organization.”

In terms of safety concerns, delaying the upgrades does not impact the safety of the public he says.

“The issues with our plant, safety is not a concern; it’s reliability. I liken it to an old car. At some point you keep replacing parts of an old car and you really just need to replace the car,” he said.

After consulting with experts, the club will try to get one more year out of the existing plant, and make repairs as needed to save the curling season.

The club has roughly 1,000 members, and curling is happening 10 to 12 hours per day, seven days a week.

“A bit more risk if something fails; we might have to cancel for a period of time; that’s the risk we’re living with,” he says.

Soldiers being treated in hospital for burns from a deadly fire at an Alberta military base have a long psychological recovery ahead of them, says an Edmonton surgeon treating some of the injured.

Dr. Josh Wong, the interim medical director of the Edmonton Firefighters Burn Treatment Unit at the University of Alberta Hospital, says recovering from such severe burns can take months or years.

“For patients who experience severe burns, recovery is often a long and challenging journey. Their care doesn’t end when they leave the ICU or even the hospital,” Wong said Thursday at a news conference at the hospital.

“Many will require ongoing treatment and rehabilitation.”

Wong, who is a plastic and reconstructive surgeon specializing in burn cases, said the mental impact from even small burns can become more intense over time.

“I have mentioned to the families that the psychological effect actually comes up stronger as they recover and become more aware later on as well,” he said. 

The Armed Forces had said that a windstorm on Oct. 17 pushed flames from a grass fire onto troops in a training exercise at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, southeast of Edmonton.

Prime Minister Mark Carney called the fire one of the worst tragedies for the Armed Forces on home soil during peacetime.

Four were killed in the fire. They have been identified as: Pte. Shaun Farrell, 23, of Prince Albert, Sask.; Pte. Aidan Goulding, 23, of North Vancouver, B.C.; Pte. Hayden Lykkemark, 19, of Langley, B.C.; and Sgt. Morgan Wong, 26, of Edmonton.

A fifth soldier, Pte. William Douglas Dal Bianco, died of his injured earlier this month while in an Ontario hospital.

RELATED: Vancouver Island mom of soldier who died in CFB Wainwright fire remembers son as ‘bright light’

About three dozen soldiers were initially injured.

Acute Care Alberta said 19 were still being cared for in provincial hospitals, with seven listed in critical condition.

The military said Saturday that two others remained in hospitals in British Columbia and Ontario, where they were transferred to be closer to their families.

Michael Suddes, interim chief operating officer for the Alberta Health Services’ Edmonton area, said officials could not provide specifics about the recovering soldiers due to patient confidentiality.

“But there is a spectrum,” he said. “Several patients, while they may be in critical condition, several (other) patients have already been discharged home.”

Dr. Sayeh Zielke, interim chief executive officer of Acute Care Alberta, said the fire put a huge stress on the province’s health-care system.

“We passed it,” she said. “We were able to manage the capacity and co-ordinate the response to provide the care, not only for the injured soldiers, but also the rest of our version that needed care.”

Zielke said health-care providers are still in the thick of treating the injured soldiers, but soon there will be a debriefing process to see if improvements can be made.

“We’re trying to do our best by every single day. So for us, it very much feels like a marathon,” she said.

“There’s always lessons to be learned, and we can always do better and aim for perfection.”

Wong said patients with severe burns require complex, intensive treatment that involves multiple procedures and surgeries, extensive rehabilitation, psychological support and ongoing followup care.

He said the Wainwright fire presented an extraordinary challenge for his team, who admitted 20 critically injured patients in a short period of time — about five times the specialized burn critical care capacity.

He added that there were already 15 other burn patients in care at the time.

“Our teams moved quickly to mobilize the physicians, the nurses, other health-care professionals with specialized training and experience needed to provide this level of care,” Wong said.

He also recognized that many health-care workers may start to feel the effects of their hard work and trauma they have witnessed, and his team is preparing for that. 

“When you’re in the midst of all the work and the adrenalin rushing and trying to help these patients, that’s where our focus is going to,” he said. 

“But we know very well that as the weeks and the months go on, there will be some effects, there will be some fatigue, there’ll be some psychological effects of these injuries.”

The family of a British Columbia woman found dead more than five years ago has filed a civil lawsuit against her husband, asking the B.C. Supreme Court to declare that he killed her.

Trina Hunt’s burned body was found in March 2021 near Hope, B.C., two months after the 48-year-old was reported missing.

Her husband Iain Hunt was charged with one count of indignity to human remains in February 2025.

Mounties have previously called the death a homicide, but no murder charges have been filed.

The notice of claim, filed Wednesday by the woman’s family, said Iain Hunt intentionally misled them and police by reporting her missing, even though he knew she was dead and where her body was hidden.

It said he “continued the charade by initially participating in a reward for information concerning Trina’s disappearance.”

The woman’s family had offered a $50,000 reward for new information leading to criminal charges.

None of the allegations against Iain Hunt have been proven in court.

The family is also asking the court to make Iain Hunt hand over any assets he inherited as a result of her death.

The lawsuit says the plaintiffs do not know if Trina Hunt had a will at the time of her death, and her husband refused to provide a copy or say whether one existed.

It notes the couple jointly purchased a home in Port Moody in 2006 for $623,230, and Iain became the sole owner when his wife died.

The filing says Hunt sold the property for more than $1.9 million and bought a new home in Harrison Mills, B.C., using those funds.

Trina’s family is seeking a certificate of pending litigation against the Harrison Mills property, as well as a tracing order for all the assets he acquired “as a result of her wrongful death.”

The lawsuit says that Iain Hunt’s actions have and continue to cause the family “mental anguish and distress, and anxiety.”

They are also seeking funds for damages, including for costs associated with Trina Hunt’s funeral and burial.

The claim says Hunt’s criminal trial is scheduled to begin next October in Port Coquitlam provincial court.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 26, 2026.
